theater: 益州成都及眉嘉邛諸州

battle.name: 王小波、李順起義
battle.theater: 益州成都及眉嘉邛諸州
battle.brief: 993年秋冬，王小波、李順在益州成都舉事，眾聚至數萬，轉攻眉州、嘉州、邛州諸城，殺稅吏、開倉散糧；宋廷先招撫後進剿，994年王小波戰歿，995年李順被擒處死。蜀地城塞多為木柵夯土，攻城靠雲梯、撞車與拋石飛石，卡面羅馬扭力投石機正是這條攻城技術的源頭。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 這場起義發生在北宋立國之初的益州，即今四川成都一帶，開戰的兩方，一方是北宋朝廷與派駐益州的軍政機構，另一方是王小波、李順率領的蜀地起義眾。起義方並非一個國家，而是以成都平原的煮鹽工、農民與船工為骨幹，靠鹽井、鹽場與鄉里關係迅速聚合的武裝隊伍；他們沒有常設編制，也沒有統一的軍令，破城之後往往散歸田間，靠口頭號令再集，頭目之間亦無嚴格的上下之屬。《宋史》與《續資治通鑑長編》都把此役列在民變一類而不是盜賊或黨爭之列，說明這不是派系之鬥，而是新附之地民眾對官府的抗爭。官方的指揮系統則是樞密院發兵、益州路帥府與成都府一級的軍馬都監、兵馬監押、押班分層節制：徵調蜀州等地的蕃兵與廂軍，再抽調京師禁軍入蜀，糧餉由川峽諸州倉儲與劍南、梓州一線的水陸轉運供應。雙方力量對比懸殊，起義方靠人數與流動，官府靠糧秣、器械與城防；正因如此，這場戰爭在編制上是雜牌對官軍，在技術上卻第一次迫使益州的官府認真面對民間的攻城器械與城防缺口。
countriesEn: This rising broke out among the people of Yizhou, the country around modern Chengdu in Sichuan, in the first years of the Northern Song. The two sides were the Song court together with the military and civil administration it stationed in Yizhou on one hand, and on the other the armed bands of the Shu country led by Wang Xiaobo and Li Shun. The rebel side was not a state: its backbone was made up of the salt-boiling workers, the peasants and the boatmen of the Chengdu plain, mustered quickly through the salt wells, the salt works and the networks of village kinship. It had no permanent establishment and no unified order of battle; after a town was taken the men would often disperse back to their fields and be reassembled on a spoken word, and there was no strict chain of command between the leaders. Both the History of Song and the Xu Zizhi Tongjian changbian class the affair among the risings of the people, not among bandits and not as a struggle of parties, which shows that this was not a contest of factions but a protest of the inhabitants of a newly annexed country against their officials. The command system of the government side ran in layers: the Bureau of Military Affairs sent the troops, and the military circuit office in Yizhou and the prefecture of Chengdu held the line through the juma dujian, the bingma jianya and the yaban, with the Fan troops and the xiang troops called up from Sizhou and other prefectures, and detachments of the imperial guards drawn down from the capital; grain and supplies came up from the granaries of the circuits of Chuanxi and by water and land along the roads of Jiannan and Zizhou. The two sides were badly matched: the rebels on numbers and on movement, the court on supplies, on siege engines and on fortifications. For that very reason the war was, in organization, an irregular force set against a regular army, while in technology it forced the authorities in Yizhou to take seriously, for the first time, the siege engines of the common people and the weak points of their own walls.
people: 王小波是這場起義的發動者。傳世記載說他是蜀地人，做煮鹽的苦工出身，平日不畏強豪，好替鄉里出頭；起事之後他自領軍眾，以均賦相號，行軍所至開倉散粟，因此聚眾極快。他的名字與王小波李順起義一起被後世記住，但關於他的家世、鄉里與年歲，諸書說法不一，記載相當有限，多數只能從《宋史》相關列傳與《涑水記聞》《東軒筆錄》的追敘中拼出輪廓，所知不過是一個熟悉鹽井與鄉里人情、又敢於揭事的人。李順是王小波最得力的同夥，一般記載說他是蜀中民間出身的匠人，與王小波結義之後在起義軍中負責統兵與傳檄，歸附者多歸於他；他也常被描述為比王小波更善於曉諭與勸降，勸得部分州縣守軍開城。至於朝廷一邊，站在最前面的是皇帝宋太宗：起事消息傳回京師之後，是否討伐、是否招撫、何時發兵入蜀、糧餉從哪一路運，都由他在宮中定奪，而蜀道艱遠、運糧不易，也讓每一道詔令都來得遲緩。事後真正收拾局面的是張詠，他於996年出任知益州，罷除苛歛、均賦、練兵、築城，把起義之後的蜀地重新整理成可以長久守禦的樣子。另有益州各州縣的守將、監軍、押班與稅吏數十人死於亂軍，姓名多不見於史；受波及的百姓不在本條目論述之列，此處只論軍政人物。
peopleEn: Wang Xiaobo was the man who set the rising going. The transmitted accounts make him a native of Shu who worked at boiling salt, a labourer of the salt furnaces, and they say that he did not bow before the strong and wealthy and liked to stand up for the people of his own village. Once the rising began he led the men himself, took the equalising of the levies as his banner, and wherever he went he opened the granaries and scattered the grain, which is why the crowds gathered so fast. His name has been handed down together with that of the rising of Wang Xiaobo and Li Shun, but his family, his home village and his age are given in a variety of ways and the material is thin; the outline can only be pieced together from the relevant biographies of the History of Song and from the retrospective notices of the Shu Water Record of Talk and the Dongxuan Biquan, and what emerges is a man who knew the salt wells and the people of the country and dared to speak out. Li Shun was Wang Xiaobo's closest associate. He is generally described as an artisan from among the common people of Shu; after joining forces with Wang he took charge of leading the troops and of the proclamations, and many of those who came over did so to him. He is also often described as better than Wang at persuasion and at inducing garrisons to surrender, and several prefectural and county garrisons are said to have opened their gates to him. On the side of the court the figure in front was the emperor, Song Taizong: once the news of the rising reached the capital, whether to punish it or to pacify it, when to send troops down into Shu and by which route the grain should travel were all decided by him in the palace, and the length of the road and the difficulty of the transport made every order arrive late. The man who put the aftermath in order was Zhang Yong, who was sent to govern Yizhou in 996, removed the harsh exactions, equalised the levies, trained the soldiers, built the walls, and so rearranged the Shu country after the rising into a shape that could be defended for long. A number of officers of the prefectures and counties of Yizhou, commanders, jianyu and yaban, and tax collectors, died in the fighting, and their names are mostly not preserved; the common people affected by the rising are not listed here, because this account deals only with troops and equipment.
kits: 卡面這件投石機是羅馬的扭力式拋石機，約公元前25年由維特魯維烏斯一波利奧記在《建築十書》之中：木製機身前端裝一根粗壯的拋臂，箭形發射槽兩側束著粗大的扭力索，絞盤把臂拉緊之後靠脫扣釋放，把臂杆蓄存的扭力轉成石彈的初速，射程約數百步，羅馬人拿它對付高牆與塔樓。它之所以出現在這張北宋初年蜀地民變的卡面上，是因為它代表把儲存的勢能換成一塊石頭這條攻城技術的源頭，而九百年後北宋在益州使用的拋石機，即宋人所稱的砲，正是這條譜系的末端：中國的砲多為木製機身配長臂與鐵鏈索具，發射的也不只是石頭，還有長杆的飛石，以連射消耗城頭的遮蔽物。《宋史·兵志》已把砲列入官軍攻城器械之列。起義軍攻城所用的更多是雲梯、撞車、飛石與簡單的竿砲，靠人抬肩扛把器械送到城下，技術門檻低、展開快；官軍平叛同樣倚賴攻城器械與城防，益州各州縣多為木柵與夯土牆，只在少數要衝設甕城與馬面。兵裝方面，蜀地守軍以皮甲、札甲為主，弓弩與長槍為主要兵器，另有大量鄉兵與蕃兵；戰馬與輜重車數量有限，糧秣依賴川峽的倉儲與劍南、梓州一線的水陸轉運。
kitsEn: The onager on the card is the Roman torsion stone-thrower, described about 25 BC by Vitruvius Pollio in the De architectura. Its wooden frame carried a stout throwing arm, and a great skein of torsion cord was bound into the two sides of the arrow-shaped throwing slot; the windlass drew the arm back, and a catch then released the weight, converting the twist stored in the arm into the initial speed of the stone. Its range was of the order of several hundred paces, and the Romans used it against high walls and towers. It is on the face of a card for a popular rising in Shu in the early Northern Song because it marks the source of the line of siege technique that turns stored potential energy into a stone, and the stone-thrower the Song used in Yizhou in 993, the pao of the Chinese, was the far end of that same line. The Chinese machines had wooden frames with long arms and iron linkages, and their ammunition was not only stone but also the long pole called the flying stone, fired in sequence to wear away the cover of a wall head; by the early Song the History of Song, in its chapter on arms, already listed the pao among the siege engines of the government army. The rebels who attacked towns relied more on the ladder, the ram, the flying stone and simple pole-throwers, carried to the foot of the wall on men's shoulders, which were cheap and quick to set up. The government relied on siege engines and on defences in the same way, for the prefectures and counties of Yizhou were mostly closed with wooden palisades and rammed earth, and only a few of the important posts had a barbican and bladed walls. In armour the garrisons of Shu wore chiefly leather and lamellar, with bows, crossbows and long spears as their principal weapons, alongside a large body of local militia and Fan troops; horses and wagons were few, and the grain depended on the granaries of Chuanxi and on the water and land roads of Jiannan and Zizhou.
tactics: 起義軍的作戰方式以流動與夜襲為主。蜀地平原村鎮密集，州縣城牆多為木柵夯土，防守兵員有限，起義眾便避開與官軍主力正面對決的戰法，只在官軍分兵或援軍未到的空檔撲向城邑：集結在鄉野、趁夜接近、架雲梯與撞車破門，破城之後殺害稅吏與欺壓鄉里的官吏，開倉散粟，再在官軍合圍之前散走。史書常記起義軍聚散無常，這既是沒有後勤體系的表現，也是他們避實擊虛的辦法。官軍的應對則分三步：第一步是招撫，遣使宣諭、許以赦免，命令起義眾解散；第二步是分進合擊，益州本地軍兵與蕃兵在前，京師禁軍與新配發的援軍在後，企圖以兵力與包圍迫其就範；第三步是攻城器械集中使用，在眉州、嘉州、邛州一線以砲與撞車破城。起義軍在攻城技術上並不生疏，州縣木柵一攻即破，這也解釋了為何官軍起初的招撫未能奏效，後來每一次進兵都必須先清剿鄉野再攻城。整場戰爭歷時約兩年，節奏是叛起、鎮壓、再叛、大軍進剿、斬首的拉鋸，最後以王小波戰歿、李順被擒告終。
tacticsEn: The way the rebels fought was built on movement and on night attacks. The villages and market towns of the Shu plain stood close together, the walls of the prefectures and counties were mostly palisade and rammed earth, and the garrisons were thin. The rebels therefore avoided any decision in the open against the main body of the government army, and struck only in the gaps when the troops were dispersed or before the relief had arrived: they mustered in the countryside, came up under cover of night, set ladders and rams against the gates, and once the town was broken they killed the tax collectors and the officials who had abused the people, opened the granaries, scattered the grain, and then dispersed before the government troops could close in. The histories often record that the rebels mustered and dispersed without constancy; that is at once the sign of an army with no logistic system and the method by which they avoided the solid and struck the empty. The government answered in three stages. First, pacification: envoys were sent out to proclaim amnesty and to order the rebels to disperse. Second, converging attacks: the soldiers of Yizhou and the Fan troops were put in front, the imperial guards and fresh reinforcements from the capital behind, in the hope that weight of numbers and encirclement would bring the rebels to terms. Third, the concentration of siege engines along the line of Meizhou, Jiazhou and Qiongzhou, where the pao and the ram were used to break the walls. The rebels were not ignorant of siegecraft, and the timber palisades of the prefectural towns fell at once, which explains why the first attempts at pacification failed and why every later advance of the government troops had to be preceded by a clearing of the countryside. The whole war ran for about two years, in the rhythm of rising, suppression, rising again, the great drive of the relieving army, and the taking of the chiefs, and it ended with the death of Wang Xiaobo and the capture of Li Shun.
data: 可核對的數字不多，而且多帶爭議。時間一端繫於淳化四年即993年，一般記在該年秋冬之交，朝廷得報在十一月；李順被擒處死在淳化五年即995年，前後約一年半到兩年。地理上，戰火主要在成都平原的益州、眉州、嘉州、邛州、蜀州、資州、普州、遂州與果州一帶，另有波及陵州與瀘州方向的消息。兵員方面，諸書多以眾至數萬形容起義眾，官軍投入的則是益州本地軍兵、蕃兵與抽調自京師的禁軍，合計亦在數萬量級，但沒有可以核對的編制表。人數以外較可靠的硬數字有兩類：第一是成都城牆，張詠在益州所築的磚石城垣是宋代留下的實物憑證，後世多推算工程起於996年前後，歷數年而成，成都地下的宋代城基至今可辨；第二是鹽法上的禁令與減賦，淳化五年之後朝廷與張詠先後更動博買與井稅，把蜀地每年所征的鹽課降下來，餘下的以均賦與丈量田畝一類的名目分攤下去。雙方死傷數字無從查考，本條目只論部隊與裝備，不作推估。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, and most of them are disputed. The dating runs from the fourth year of Chunhua, 993, generally placed in the late autumn and early winter of that year, with the court learning of it in the eleventh month. Li Shun was taken and put to death in the fifth year of Chunhua, 995, so the affair lasted something between a year and a half and two years. Geographically the fighting lay in the Chengdu plain, across Yizhou, Meizhou, Jiazhou, Qiongzhou, Shuzhou, Zhizhou, Puzhou, Suizhou and Guozhou, with reports also coming in from the directions of Lingzhou and Luzhou. As for numbers of men, the books generally describe the rebel crowds as reaching tens of thousands, and the government committed the soldiers of Yizhou, the Fan troops and detachments of the imperial guards drawn from the capital, again on the scale of tens of thousands, but no table of establishment survives that can be checked. Beyond headcounts there are two kinds of harder figure. The first is the wall of Chengdu: the brick-and-stone enceinte built by Zhang Yong while he governed Yizhou is the material evidence the Song left behind, the work is generally reckoned to have begun about 996 and to have taken several years, and the Song foundations under modern Chengdu can still be traced. The second is on the salt side, in the orders and the reductions after the rising: after Chunhua five the court, and then Zhang Yong, in turn revised the compulsory purchase of salt and the tax on the wells, lowered the salt levy taken from Shu each year, and shared what remained under names such as the equal levy and the survey of the acres. No figures survive for the losses on either side, and this entry speaks only of troops and equipment and offers no estimate.
cause: 起義的直接原因，是蜀地鹽法與差役的苛急。宋初朝廷平蜀之後，把益州鹽井收歸榷鹽，由鹽運司統籌：官府以低價向井戶博買所產之鹽，再高價售出，井戶既失去自主，又被攤派井稅與身丁錢；鹽井一旦枯竭，額數不減，官吏催督更急，農戶被迫逃亡或聚眾抗鬪。與此同時，蜀地百姓被大量徵發入京充禁軍，服役與遠役的負擔也壓在尋常民戶身上。乾德以來蜀地屢見水旱歉收，糧價騰貴，而官倉積粟卻不時發放，饑民無從得食；起義者提出的均賦、救民與有粟不發一類說法，正切中這層怨情。政治上則是另一層：新附之地二十八年仍受舊官員與軍將歧視，蜀人好勇、聚族而居，極易被一兩名敢於揭事的人號召；同時代別處已有小股抗爭，益州等地的鬥毆、鹽井罷工與盜賊記載，都可以看作這場大起義的前奏。至於引爆的具體事件，究竟是某一口鹽井的稅額糾紛，還是某次官吏催督引發的衝突，史無明文，各家說法並存，難以斷定。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the rising was the harshness of the salt law and of the levies in Shu. After the court had taken Shu in the first years of the Song, the salt wells of Yizhou were brought under the state monopoly and administered by the salt transport office. The government bought the salt of the well owners at a low price under the name of the compulsory purchase and then sold it at a high one, so the well owners lost their own market and were assessed with the well tax and the head tax on top. When a well ran dry the quota did not fall, the officials pressed harder, and the peasant households fled or rose in anger. At the same time the people of Shu were levied in large numbers for the imperial guards in the capital, and the burden of service and of distant duty fell on ordinary households. From the Qiande era onwards there were repeated droughts and poor harvests in Shu, grain prices rose, and yet the granaries of the officials were not opened in time, so that the hungry could not get food. The cries of the equal levy, of rescue for the people, and of grain in store that was not given out were aimed exactly at this resentment. Politically there was a second layer. For twenty-eight years the newly annexed country was still treated with contempt by the old officials and the military commanders; the Shu people were bold and lived in great clan groups, and could be mustered at once by one or two men willing to speak out. There had already been small disturbances elsewhere in the era, and the records of affrays, of salt workers striking and of robbery in Yizhou and elsewhere can all be read as the prelude to this great rising. As for the particular spark, whether it was a dispute over the tax of one salt well or a clash provoked by the officials pressing for their dues, the histories are silent, the versions differ, and the point cannot be settled.
impact: 這場起義是北宋立國之後第一次大規模的民變，也是後來南宋四川民變的一個預警。直接後果有三層。第一，蜀地鹽法被徹底檢視：起義平定之後，朝廷不得不減免博買、放寬井稅、整肅鹽運司官吏，張詠出知益州之後更把按畝均賦付諸實行，鹽利與民力之間的矛盾暫時緩和，但根本的解法要到王安石變法的鹽法改制才真正觸及。第二，軍防與城防被重做：張詠在益州練兵、置備攻城器械、築起成都城，把前此的竹木柵城改為磚石城垣，成都地下的宋代城基即其見證；蜀地從此以城自守、兵自練的方式應付內部變亂，而不必等待京師的援軍。第三，對統治觀念的刺激：起義顯示新附之地的民怨不能只靠鎮壓，北宋此後在川峽一帶以招撫為主、兵威為輔，並把民變正式列入邊防與刑名兩套文書之中。起義者本身多為煮鹽工與鄉民，旋即潰散，不構成組織化的勢力，因此這場戰爭的歷史意義不在於推翻朝廷，而在於第一次暴露了鹽業壟斷與新附治理之間那道一直沒有被處理的裂縫。
impactEn: This rising was the first mass revolt of the people after the founding of the Song, and it was a warning of the popular risings that Shu would see again in the Southern Song. There were three layers of consequence. First, the salt law of Shu was put under review. After the rising was put down the court had to reduce the compulsory purchase, relax the tax on the wells, and purge the officials of the salt transport office; Zhang Yong, on taking up the government of Yizhou, carried the equalisation of the levies by acre into practice, so that the conflict between the salt revenue and the strength of the people was eased for a time, though the real solution was not reached until the salt reforms of Wang Anshi's New Policies. Second, the military and urban defences of the country were remade. Zhang Yong trained troops, equipped siege engines and built the city of Chengdu, replacing the earlier bamboo-and-timber palisade with a brick-and-stone enceinte, of which the Song foundations under modern Chengdu are the witness; from then on Shu met internal disorder by the motto of the city defending itself and the troops trained by themselves, instead of waiting for reinforcements from the capital. Third, there was a shock to the idea of rule. The rising showed that the resentment of a newly annexed country could not be managed by repression alone, and the Song thereafter carried on pacification as the first principle in the circuits of Chuanxi, with armed force only in support, and entered the rising of the people into both the frontier regulations and the penal codes. The rebels themselves were salt workers and villagers who dispersed at once and never formed an organised force, so the historical meaning of the rising lay not in any attempt to overturn the court, but in the first exposure of the crack between the salt monopoly and the government of a newly annexed people.
result: 淳化四年秋，王小波、李順在益州舉事，眾以煮鹽工與鄉民為主，轉戰成都、眉州、嘉州、邛州一帶，殺害官吏、開倉散粟，把均賦的口號喊到路盡人皆知。官軍初戰不利，之後由京師調禁軍入蜀，與益州兵、蕃兵合兵進剿；994年，王小波在戰陣中歿，傳說中箭之後又被剖分示眾，起義由此崩解，餘眾退保。995年，李順在嘉州一帶被擒，官軍將其解送京師，凌遲處死，蜀地的局勢才告平息。事後的收拾工作比戰事本身更長：朝廷下詔自責、減免蜀中鹽課、整頓鹽運司，張詠於996年出任知益州，續行均賦、練兵，築起成都的磚城。於是這一場起義的結局可以這樣概括：軍事上以鎮壓收場，起義首領一死於陣、一誅於市；制度上卻換來一次難得的整改，蜀地的鹽法與城防為其後一百五十年的穩定打下了基礎。而史書留下的一句話同樣留給後人：民怨若積到要燒城、要攻城的地步，靠招撫是壓不住的，必須真的把井稅與差役改掉。
resultEn: In the autumn of the fourth year of Chunhua, Wang Xiaobo and Li Shun raised the banner in Yizhou, their following made up chiefly of salt workers and villagers, and they moved through Chengdu, Meizhou, Jiazhou and Qiongzhou, killing officials, opening the granaries and scattering grain, until the cry of the equal levy was heard on every road. The government army did badly at first; reinforcements were then drawn from the capital and joined with the soldiers of Yizhou and the Fan troops in a converging drive. In 994 Wang Xiaobo fell on the field, and the story goes that he was struck by an arrow and his body was then cut up and displayed, and the rising fell apart with him, the survivors falling back. In 995 Li Shun was taken in the country about Jiazhou and carried to the capital, where he was cut down piece by piece; only then was the situation in Shu settled. The tidying up took longer than the fighting. The court issued a self-reproach, reduced the salt levy of Shu and reformed the salt transport office, and in 996 Zhang Yong was sent to govern Yizhou, where he continued the equalisation of the levies, trained the soldiers and raised the brick wall of Chengdu. The outcome of the rising can therefore be put in this way. Militarily it ended in suppression, with one chief dead on the field and the other executed; institutionally it brought about a rare and far-reaching reform, since the salt law and the defences of Shu gained the basis of a century and a half of stability. And the histories left behind a caution for posterity: when the resentment of the people has grown to the point of burning towns and storming walls, pacification will not hold it down; the tax on the wells and the burden of service have to be changed for real.
